templates.subtopic: Describe and continue sequences
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S1 Describe and continue sequences
templates.text: Write the next two terms of the sequence [[s]], [[s + d]], [[s + 2 * d]], [[s + 3 * d]], …

templates.subtopic: Describe and continue sequences
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S1 Describe and continue sequences
templates.text: Write the next two terms of the sequence [[s]], [[s * m]], [[s * m * m]], [[s * m * m * m]], …
templates.answer: [[s * m * m * m * m]], [[s * m * m * m * m * m]] (multiply by [[m]] each time)

templates.subtopic: Describe and continue sequences
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S1 Describe and continue sequences
templates.text: Is the sequence [[s]], [[s + d]], [[s + 3 * d]], [[s + 6 * d]] arithmetic, geometric or neither? Explain.
templates.answer: Neither: the differences are [[d]], [[2 * d]], [[3 * d]], which are not constant, and there is no common multiplier

templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S3 Describe and continue sequences involving surds (E)
templates.text: A geometric sequence has first term [[a]] and second term $[[a]]\sqrt{[[b]]}$. Show that the 3rd term is [[a * b]] and find the 5th term. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Ratio $\sqrt{[[b]]}$; 3rd term [[a * b]]; 5th term [[a * b * b]]

templates.subtopic: Generate a sequence given an algebraic rule
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S4 Generate a sequence given an algebraic rule
templates.text: The $n$th term of a sequence is $n^2 + [[c]]$. Which term is equal to [[k * k + c]]?
templates.answer: Term number [[k]] (since [[k * k + c]] − [[c]] = [[k * k]] and $[[k]]^2 = [[k * k]]$)

templates.text: A sequence has the $n$th term $[[d]]n[[c|signed]]$. Find the 20th term. Then use the $n$th term to say whether [[t]] is in the sequence.
templates.answer: 20th term: [[20 * d + c]]; [[t]] [[(t - c) % d == 0|if:is/is not]] in the sequence

templates.subtopic: Algebraic arguments and proof
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B4 Sequences and proof · S8 Algebraic arguments and proof
templates.text: Prove that $n^2 + n$ is always even. Check with $n = [[n]]$.
templates.answer: $n^2 + n = n(n + 1)$, a product of consecutive integers, so one factor is even; [[n * n + n]] is even
